27895: and, having cast off the anchors, they left [them] in the sea, at the same time loosening the lashings of the rudders, and hoisting the foresail to the wind, they made for the strand.
27896: And falling into a place where two seas met they ran the ship aground, and the prow having stuck itself fast remained unmoved, but the stern was broken by the force of the waves.
27900: And when we got safe [to land] we then knew that the island was called Melita.
27901: But the barbarians shewed us no common kindness; for, having kindled a fire, they took us all in because of the rain that was falling and because of the cold.
27903: And when the barbarians saw the beast hanging from his hand, they said to one another, This man is certainly a murderer, whom, [though] saved out of the sea, Nemesis has not allowed to live.
27905: But they expected that he would have swollen or fallen down suddenly dead. But when they had expected a long time and saw nothing unusual happen to him, changing their opinion, they said he was a god.
27906: Now in the country surrounding that place were the lands belonging to the chief man of the island, by name Publius, who received us and gave [us] hospitality three days in a very friendly way.
27907: And it happened that the father of Publius lay ill of fever and dysentery; to whom Paul entered in, and having prayed and laid his hands on him cured him.
27910: And after three months we sailed in a ship which had wintered in the island, an Alexandrian, with [the] Dioscuri for its ensign.
27911: And having come to Syracuse we remained three days.
27912: Whence, going in a circuitous course, we arrived at Rhegium; and after one day, the wind having changed to south, on the second day we came to Puteoli,
27914: And thence the brethren, having heard about us, came to meet us as far as Appii Forum and Tres Tabernae, whom when Paul saw, he thanked God and took courage.
27915: And when we came to Rome, [the centurion delivered up the prisoners to the praetorian prefect, but] Paul was allowed to remain by himself with the soldier who kept him.
27922: And having appointed him a day many came to him to the lodging, to whom he expounded, testifying of the kingdom of God, and persuading them concerning Jesus, both from the law of Moses and the prophets, from early morning to evening.
27924: And being disagreed among themselves they left; Paul having spoken one word, Well spoke the Holy Spirit through Esaias the prophet to our fathers,
27930: preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ, with all freedom unhinderedly.
27931: Paul, bondman of Jesus Christ, [a] called apostle, separated to God’s glad tidings,

27941: For I greatly desire to see you, that I may impart to you some spiritual gift to establish you;
27942: that is, to have mutual comfort among you, each by the faith [which is] in the other, both yours and mine.
27945: so, as far as depends on me, am I ready to announce the glad tidings to you also who [are] in Rome.
27947: for righteousness of God is revealed therein, on the principle of faith, to faith: according as it is written, But the just shall live by faith.

27952: professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,
27953: and changed the glory of the incorruptible God into [the] likeness of an image of corruptible man and of birds and quadrupeds and reptiles.
27956: For this reason God gave them up to vile lusts; for both their females changed the natural use into that contrary to nature;
27957: and in like manner the males also, leaving the natural use of the female, were inflamed in their lust towards one another; males with males working shame, and receiving in themselves the recompense of their error which was fit.
27959: being filled with all unrighteousness, wickedness, covetousness, malice; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, evil dispositions; whisperers,
27960: back-biters, hateful to God, insolent, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents,
27961: void of understanding, faithless, without natural affection, unmerciful;
27963: Therefore thou art inexcusable, O man, every one who judgest, for in that in which thou judgest another, thou condemnest thyself; for thou that judgest doest the same things.
27965: And thinkest thou this, O man, who judgest those that do such things, and practisest them [thyself], that thou shalt escape the judgment of God?
27966: or despisest thou the riches of his goodness, and forbearance, and long-suffering, not knowing that the goodness of God leads thee to repentance?
27967: but, according to thy hardness and impenitent heart, treasurest up to thyself wrath, in [the] day of wrath and revelation of [the] righteous judgment of God,
27969: to them who, in patient continuance of good works, seek for glory and honour and incorruptibility, life eternal.

27977: who shew the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearing witness, and their thoughts accusing or else excusing themselves between themselves;)
27979: But if thou art named a Jew, and restest in the law, and makest thy boast in God,
27980: and knowest the will, and discerningly approvest the things that are more excellent, being instructed out of the law;
27983: thou then that teachest another, dost thou not teach thyself? thou that preachest not to steal, dost thou steal?
27984: thou that sayest [man should] not commit adultery, dost thou commit adultery? thou that abhorrest idols, dost thou commit sacrilege?
27987: For circumcision indeed profits if thou keep [the] law; but if thou be a law-transgressor, thy circumcision is become uncircumcision.
27988: If therefore the uncircumcision keep the requirements of the law, shall not his uncircumcision be reckoned for circumcision,
27991: but he [is] a Jew [who is so] inwardly; and circumcision, of the heart, in spirit, not in letter; whose praise [is] not of men, but of God.
27992: What then [is] the superiority of the Jew? or what the profit of circumcision?
27996: But if our unrighteousness commend God’s righteousness, what shall we say? Is God unrighteous who inflicts wrath? I speak according to man.
27998: For if the truth of God, in my lie, has more abounded to his glory, why yet am I also judged as a sinner?
27999: and not, according as we are injuriously charged, and according as some affirm that we say, Let us practise evil things, that good ones may come? whose judgment is just.
